title: Standstill Reversal, Paired Snap, Typed Measure, Lit Links & Known Slots
description: Five features that delete something you tracked by hand: animation direction, snap target, column width, click source, slot content.

drops.title: Reverse From a Standstill
drops.description: Firefox 157 makes reverse() act on an animation parked at playbackRate 0, and mirrors startTime when a scroll-driven animation flips sign.
drops.concept: Setting playbackRate to 0 is the honest way to freeze an animation mid-flight, but reverse() used to be swallowed in that state — rate stayed 0 and nothing moved. Firefox 157 fixed that, and fixed the related case where flipping the sign of playbackRate on a scroll-driven animation left startTime stranded instead of mirroring it to the other end of the timeline. The demo probes your engine live and says which behaviour you are looking at.
drops.source: MDN Web Docs — Firefox 157 release notes for developers

interaction.mouse: Freeze a running animation at rate 0, then reverse it; flip the sign of a scroll-driven animation and watch startTime mirror
interaction.click: Play / Freeze / reverse() per lane, plus reverse-all and set-rate-zero on nine chips at once
interaction.touch: Scroll the inner box to drive lane 2; all controls are 40px tap targets

drops.title: Snapping to One Thing
drops.description: scroll-snap-type: pair lands both axes of a two-axis scroller on the same element instead of letting each axis pick its own.
drops.concept: With scroll-snap-type: both, the horizontal and vertical axes choose their snap targets independently. On an off-grid board that means you can settle with x aligned to one card and y aligned to another, framing the gap between them. Chrome 156's pair keyword makes the second axis follow whichever element the first one chose, so every rest position frames a whole card.
drops.source: Chrome Platform Status — Chrome 156 release notes

interaction.mouse: Trackpad or shift+wheel to scroll each board diagonally; the readout names whichever card is inside the centre frame
interaction.click: Cards light up when they are the framed element
interaction.touch: Two-finger drag on either board; the fallback re-snaps after the scroll settles

drops.title: Type That Counts Its Own Pixels
drops.description: Dividing a container width by 1px yields a plain number, so weight, tracking and leading can respond to the box with no clamp stack.
drops.concept: CSS typed arithmetic allows a value to be divided by another of the same type, and the result is a unitless number: calc(100cqi / 1px) is literally how many pixels wide the container is. Feed that into font-weight, letter-spacing or line-height and the type reacts continuously to its own column rather than to viewport breakpoints. The divisor carries the meaning — divide by 1em to count ems, or by 320px to get a 0–1 ratio.

interaction.mouse: Drag the native resize handle on any card, or the width slider in the glass panel
interaction.click: Each card prints the pixel count CSS computed for itself, via a counter fed the same expression
interaction.touch: Width slider replaces the resize handles below 620px

drops.title: The Link That Stays Lit
drops.description: :navigation-source matches the link, button or form that started the current navigation — and keeps matching it until the navigation ends.
drops.concept: Which thumbnail did the user click? Until now only script knew: you listened for navigate, read NavigateEvent.sourceElement and tagged the element yourself. Chrome 156 ships :navigation-source so the press state — and the view-transition-name that morphs a thumbnail into a hero — can both be declarations that survive for the whole navigation.
drops.source: bram.us — “Styling the Navigation: Declarative Route and Navigation Matching in CSS”

interaction.mouse: Click a thumbnail: it keeps its ring and glow while the same-document navigation and its view transition run
interaction.click: Six real links to #card-n; a checkbox slows the transition 4× so the lit state is easy to watch
interaction.touch: Full-width card grid and a static control panel on phones

drops.title: Slots That Know They're Empty
drops.description: :has-slotted matches a slot that actually got content, so a component can collapse its optional regions from its own stylesheet.
drops.concept: An empty optional slot still occupies its padding, divider and gap, and :empty cannot help because it describes the slot's own children rather than the content assigned to it. :has-slotted matches a slot with assigned light-DOM content, so a card component can hide its badge, media and footer regions itself. Native in Firefox 136 and up; elsewhere this page falls back to a slotchange shim.

interaction.mouse: Toggle the badge, media and footer slots on the middle card and watch the regions collapse
interaction.click: Checkboxes add and remove real light-DOM children; the panel reports each slot's live state
interaction.touch: Controls stack above the cards below 620px
